definition: To make someone feel nervous or lose their confidence.

collocations.example: Her calm stare began to unnerve her opponent.
The strange noises completely unnerve the night guard.

definition: Not aware of what you are doing or what is happening around you.

collocations.example: He became an unwitting accomplice in the fraud.
She was the unwitting victim of their scheme.

definition: The way a child is cared for and taught as he or she grows up.

collocations.example: His strict upbringing made him very disciplined.
She had a happy childhood and religious upbringing.

definition: To cover a chair or sofa with soft padding and fabric.

collocations.example: They decided to upholster the old chair in leather.
It costs a lot to upholster a large sofa.

definition: An area of high land, away from rivers and the sea.

collocations.example: Deer roam freely across the upland forest here.
Many birds nest in the upland areas near wetlands.

definition: In the direction opposite to the way a river flows, toward its source.

collocations.example: Salmon struggle to swim upstream to lay eggs.
We camped on the upstream side of the rock.

definition: Designed to be practical and useful rather than beautiful.

collocations.example: The office had a plain, utilitarian design throughout.
These utilitarian objects serve a clear practical purpose.

definition: Greatest; the most possible.

collocations.example: This is a matter of the utmost importance.
Handle the fragile vase with the utmost care.

definition: An imaginary place or society where everything is perfect.

collocations.example: The author imagined a peaceful utopia without any crime.
Their plan to build a utopia soon failed.

definition: In stories, a dead person who rises at night to drink people's blood.

collocations.example: The vampire in the movie feared bright sunlight.
Old legends describe the vampire drinking human blood.

definition: The leading position in a new development, movement, or trend.

collocations.example: The company is in the vanguard of scientific progress.
These students were in the vanguard of political change.

definition: A sweet flavoring made from the pods of a tropical plant, used in food.

collocations.example: She added vanilla extract to the cake batter.
I ordered a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

definition: A position that gives a good or clear view of something.

collocations.example: From his vantage point he saw the entire valley.
The hill offered a commanding vantage over the town.

definition: A clear liquid painted onto wood to give it a hard, shiny surface.

collocations.example: The clear varnish gave the wooden table a glossy finish.
He applied a second coat of varnish carefully.

definition: To change direction suddenly, especially while moving.

collocations.example: The car suddenly veered off the main road.
The truck veered sharply to avoid the cyclist.

definition: Showing very strong, passionate feelings or opinions.

collocations.example: He was vehement in his opposition to the plan.
She made a vehement denial of the charges.

definition: Relating to Venice, a city in Italy, or its people.

collocations.example: Venetian merchants traded silk across the Mediterranean region.
She admired the beautiful Venetian glass in the shop.

definition: The act of harming someone in return for harm they caused; revenge.

collocations.example: He swore vengeance on his brother's killer.
She vowed to take vengeance for the insult.

definition: Poisonous liquid that some snakes and insects produce when they bite or sting.

collocations.example: The snake's venom can kill a person quickly.
Scientists study deadly venom to create new medicines.

definition: To compete eagerly with others to get or achieve something.

collocations.example: Several companies vie for the same contract.
The two brothers vie with each other constantly.

definition: To prove that someone or something is right or free from blame.

collocations.example: The new evidence finally vindicated her good name.
New evidence finally vindicated the accused man.

definition: A strong plastic used to make flooring, records, and protective coverings.

collocations.example: The kitchen has easy-to-clean vinyl flooring.
He collects old music on vinyl records.

definition: A bluish-purple color.

collocations.example: The evening sky turned a deep violet.
The garden was full of soft violet petals.

definition: Caused by or relating to a virus.

collocations.example: A viral infection left her too weak to work.
Doctors cannot cure a viral disease with antibiotics.

definition: A strong, clear alcoholic drink originally from Russia.

collocations.example: He poured himself a large glass of vodka.
She ordered a vodka and tonic at the bar.

definition: A fashion or style that is popular at a particular time.

collocations.example: Pale colors are very much in vogue this season.
Vintage clothing has come into vogue again.

definition: A speech sound made with the mouth open, such as a, e, i, o, or u.

collocations.example: The student practiced making a new vowel sound.
This word contains a long vowel in the middle.

definition: Rude, offensive, or showing a lack of good taste.

collocations.example: The comedian was criticized for his vulgar language.
She was offended by his vulgar joke.

definition: To move something, especially a tail, quickly from side to side.

collocations.example: Dogs wag their tails when they are happy.
The teacher began to wag a warning finger.

definition: The explosive part at the front of a missile or torpedo.

collocations.example: The missile carried a powerful nuclear warhead.
Engineers tested the missile warhead in the desert.

definition: An event or period that marks an important turning point or change.

collocations.example: The election was a watershed in the nation's history.
That discovery marked a watershed moment in medicine.

definition: A unit for measuring electrical power.

collocations.example: This room needs a brighter 100-watt bulb.
The heater uses two thousand watts of power.

definition: To hit someone or something hard.

collocations.example: You really have to whack the ball hard.
He tried to whack the nail with a hammer.

definition: The place where a person or thing is located.

collocations.example: She refused to reveal her daughter's whereabouts.
The suspect's whereabouts remain completely unknown.

definition: A sudden wish or idea, especially one that seems unreasonable.

collocations.example: We decided to travel to Spain on a whim.
He patiently indulged his young child's every whim.

definition: To shout loudly with joy or excitement.

collocations.example: The fans began to whoop with joy.
The crowd began to whoop loudly as she scored.

definition: Feeling or showing quiet sadness about something you wish you had.

collocations.example: She gave a wistful look at her old home.
He spoke with a wistful smile about his childhood.

definition: The organ in a woman's body where a baby grows before birth.

collocations.example: The baby's sense of smell develops in the womb.
The scan showed the baby in the mother's womb.

definition: Covered with growing trees.

collocations.example: The fighting took place in a densely wooded area.
They built a cabin in a quiet wooded valley.

definition: A period of physical exercise done to improve fitness.

collocations.example: She goes for an intense workout every morning.
His daily workout helps him burn fat and build muscle.

definition: Extreme anger.

collocations.example: The sinners feared the divine wrath of God.
He trembled as he faced his father's wrath.

definition: A ring of flowers or leaves, used as a decoration or to honor the dead.

collocations.example: The queen laid a wreath at the war memorial.
They hung a Christmas wreath on the front door.

definition: To twist and turn your body with small, quick movements.

collocations.example: The child tried to wriggle free from her grasp.
The worm began to wriggle across the wet soil.

definition: To twist and squeeze wet cloth to remove the water.

collocations.example: He turned away to wring out the wet shirt.
She tried to wring the water from the towel.

definition: An official legal document that orders someone to do or not do something.

collocations.example: The court issued a writ against the company.
Lawyers prepared to serve a writ on him.

definition: Made or shaped by hammering or working metal.

collocations.example: The gates were made of heavy wrought iron.
The jewelry was beautifully wrought by a skilled artisan.

definition: A thick, slightly sour food made from milk with added bacteria.

collocations.example: She bought some plain yogurt for breakfast.
The children shared a cup of frozen yogurt.

definition: A bluish-white metal used to coat other metals and to make alloys.

collocations.example: Zinc is used to protect steel from rust.
The sunscreen contains zinc oxide to block sunlight.

definition: Surprised or shocked, used in the phrase "taken aback."

collocations.example: She was completely taken aback by his anger.
We were taken aback by her hostile reaction.

definition: To hate something very much.

collocations.example: Most people abhor violence of any kind.
She abhors the idea of killing animals for sport.

definition: To choose not to do or have something, especially something enjoyable.

collocations.example: Several members chose to abstain from voting.
Doctors advised him to abstain from alcohol.

definition: The practice of not doing or having something enjoyable, such as alcohol.

collocations.example: The doctor recommended total abstinence from alcohol.
His abstinence from sweets helped him lose weight.

definition: The act of gaining a position of power or joining a group or organization.

collocations.example: Her accession to the throne was widely celebrated.
His accession to power followed a bitter election.

definition: A person who helps another person commit a crime.

collocations.example: He became an unwitting accomplice in the fraud.
The thief escaped with the help of an accomplice.

definition: Relating to sound or the sense of hearing.

collocations.example: Engineers measured the acoustic waves in the hall.
The studio has excellent acoustic insulation on its walls.

definition: A substance, such as glue, used to stick things together.

collocations.example: She used a strong adhesive to fix the tile.
The doctor closed the cut with a liquid adhesive.

definition: Something added to another thing but not an essential part of it.

collocations.example: Physical therapy is a useful adjunct to the treatment.
The app serves as an adjunct to the printed textbook.

definition: Able to be accepted or allowed, especially as evidence in court.

collocations.example: The photographs were accepted as admissible evidence.
Such confessions are not always admissible in court.

definition: A building material made of clay and straw dried in the sun.

collocations.example: They lived in an old adobe house without electricity.
The walls were built from sun-dried adobe bricks.

definition: Floating on water rather than sinking.

collocations.example: We bailed water frantically to keep the boat afloat.
The wooden raft stayed afloat for several hours.

definition: At, near, or toward the back of a ship or aircraft.

collocations.example: The sailor went aft to steer the ship.
The cabins are located fore and aft.

definition: Relating to farming, farmland, or farming communities.

collocations.example: The country was once a largely agrarian society.
The government introduced sweeping agrarian reforms.

definition: A branch of mathematics that uses letters and symbols to represent numbers.

collocations.example: Algebra is not easy, but it is very useful.
Students study linear algebra at the university.

definition: Burning; on fire.

collocations.example: Several buildings were set alight during the riot.
The dry grass quickly caught alight in the heat.

definition: The quality of being attractive or exciting.

collocations.example: The game has completely lost its allure for him.
Few can resist the allure of a tropical beach.

definition: An indirect or brief reference to something.

collocations.example: Her poetry is full of obscure literary allusion.
His speech contained a clear allusion to the scandal.

definition: High up in the air or in the sky.

collocations.example: He proudly held the trophy aloft for everyone.
The balloon drifted high aloft above the fields.

definition: Not friendly or willing to take part; distant in manner.

collocations.example: He seemed cold and remained aloof at the party.
She kept aloof from the other new students.

definition: To combine two or more things to form one single organization or unit.

collocations.example: They decided to amalgamate the two small schools.
The small firm will amalgamate with a larger one.

definition: Friendly and pleasant.

collocations.example: The new manager is an amiable, easygoing person.
She greeted the guests in an amiable manner.

definition: Not quite right; wrong.

collocations.example: Their instincts warned them that something was amiss.
The inspector found nothing amiss with the building.

definition: An ampere, a unit for measuring electric current.

collocations.example: This appliance needs a new 13-amp fuse.
Check the amp rating before connecting the device.

definition: The maximum amount by which a wave or vibration moves from its central position.

collocations.example: The amplitude of the sound wave was very large.
A louder noise generally has a greater amplitude.

definition: To cut off a part of the body, usually in a medical operation.

collocations.example: The surgeons had to amputate his injured leg.
Doctors decided to amputate the badly damaged limb.

definition: Using a continuously changing physical signal rather than digital data.

collocations.example: Old televisions received an analogue signal through an antenna.
The museum displays an early analogue computer from the 1950s.

definition: The people from whom a person is descended; family origins.

collocations.example: She traced her ancestry back three hundred years.
The two species share a common ancestry.

definition: Again, especially in a new or different way.

collocations.example: After the divorce, she decided to begin anew.
He felt born anew after the long recovery.

definition: Strong feelings of hatred or hostility.

collocations.example: There is long-standing animosity between the two nations.
She felt deep animosity toward her former boss.

definition: To destroy something completely.

collocations.example: These weapons could annihilate the entire city.
The army threatened to annihilate the enemy forces.

definition: A fixed sum of money paid to someone each year, typically for life.

collocations.example: He received a small annuity of one hundred dollars.
Investors may put some money into an annuity.

definition: Active hostility or opposition between people or groups.

collocations.example: There is still much antagonism between the rival groups.
Years of mutual antagonism divided the two families.

definition: A thing or event that existed or happened before another.

collocations.example: This tradition has historical antecedents in ancient Rome.
The modern computer had many simpler antecedents.

definition: Situated at or toward the front of something, opposite of posterior.

collocations.example: The doctor examined the anterior part of the knee.
The muscle attaches to the anterior surface of the bone.

definition: A collection of poems, stories, or other writings in one book.

collocations.example: This poem appears in a famous poetry anthology.
She edited an anthology of modern short stories.

definition: A silly or amusing act or piece of behavior.

collocations.example: The children laughed at the clown's comic antics.
His childish antics annoyed the whole office.

definition: A substance that stops the harmful effects of a poison.

collocations.example: There is no known antidote to this poison.
Doctors quickly gave the patient an effective antidote.

definition: A substance that causes the body's immune system to produce antibodies.

collocations.example: The vaccine introduces a harmless antigen into the body.
The immune system attacks any foreign antigen it detects.

definition: A narrow opening, hole, or gap.

collocations.example: Light entered the room through a narrow aperture.
He peered at the daylight through the aperture in the wall.

definition: The top or highest point of something.

collocations.example: They placed a flag at the apex of the roof.
The climbers finally reached the sharp apex of the mountain.

definition: For or to each one; each.

collocations.example: The apples cost one dollar apiece at the market.
He gave the waiting children two cookies apiece.

definition: To add something to the end of a piece of writing or a document.

collocations.example: Please append your signature to the end of the letter.
The program will append the new data to the file.

definition: Large or important enough to be noticed.

collocations.example: The new rules make no appreciable difference to most people.
There was an appreciable amount of damage to the car.

definition: Worried or nervous that something bad might happen.

collocations.example: People are still very apprehensive about the future.
She felt slightly apprehensive before the job interview.

definition: A natural ability or skill to do something well.

collocations.example: She showed a natural aptitude for learning languages.
Candidates must pass an aptitude test before hiring.
